slide09.title: Background Modeling with GPR

panels.heading: Correlation distance
panels.copy: Larger ℓ → broader variations in log mass.

panels.heading: Bin-count noise
panels.copy: α ≈ 1/y; noisier bins constrain the fit less.

slide09.notes: C is prior point variance and sqrt(C) is its SD, not event-count normalization. α is fixed by the count rule, not a third optimized kernel parameter. ℓ is distinct from the mass resolution. The drawings are illustrative.

whole_slide_script_options.label: Concise, about 30 seconds
whole_slide_script_options.script: These three panels separate the roles of the GP parameters. ℓ sets how far background variations stay correlated in log mass. C sets their variance in the latent log rate. α describes counting noise: approximately one over each bin count, so noisier bins constrain the fit less. We optimize C and ℓ on the sidebands; α follows the count rule. The curves illustrate these roles, rather than showing an HPS fit.

whole_slide_script_options.label: Intuitive, about 60 seconds
whole_slide_script_options.script:
Think of the background as a smooth trend inferred from noisy histogram bins. The length scale ℓ tells us how far one fluctuation carries information: a larger ℓ links more widely separated masses and produces broader variations. Because the coordinate is log mass, that distance is a fractional change in mass, not a fixed number of MeV.

C controls the size of the allowed fluctuations in the log rate. Increasing C changes their amplitude, while keeping ℓ fixed leaves the correlation distance unchanged. Finally, α describes how noisy each measured bin is. High-count bins have smaller relative noise and constrain the trend more strongly; low-count bins get less weight. C and ℓ are fitted from sidebands. α comes from the count rule, rather than being another adjustable kernel parameter.

whole_slide_script_options.label: Technical, about 90 seconds
whole_slide_script_options.script:
We fit log counts as a function of log mass with this squared-exponential covariance. The length scale ℓ controls the falloff with separation: at a log-mass distance of one ℓ, the correlation is exp minus one-half, about 0.61. Thus ℓ describes the fractional mass scale of background variation; it is distinct from the detector’s resonance resolution.

At zero separation the kernel equals C. C is therefore the prior variance of the latent log rate, and its square root is the corresponding standard deviation. It controls covariance amplitude, not the normalization of the event histogram. Scaling C alone does not change the normalized correlation curve.

For the observed bins, we add α to the covariance diagonal. Propagating Poisson count variance through the logarithm gives α approximately equal to one over the count for positive bins. This is why a noisier bin pulls the prediction less strongly. The zero-count case has an explicit finite floor. We optimize C and ℓ using the allowed sidebands, while recomputing α from the observed counts. The three panels isolate these effects schematically; they are not three alternative fits to the data.

new_before_source15.title: How we test the background model
new_before_source15.subtitle: Can the procedure create a false signal, absorb a true one, or misstate its error?

rows.heading: Generate independent source models
rows.body: Fit smooth analytic spectra; fluctuate background counts at the tested exposures.

rows.heading: Repeat the complete extraction
rows.body: Fit the GP sidebands, then extract a signed signal yield from background-only and injected toys.

rows.heading: Check bias, uncertainty and recovery
rows.body: Use mean pulls, pull widths and paired injected-yield response; inspect threshold and support dependence.

new_before_source15.footer: Sideband fit quality and held-out signal recovery test different parts of the procedure.
notes: The historical validation refits GP hyperparameters. The later v5.9.5 frozen-kernel audit is a separate conditional study.
Revised slide 14 uses in-sample sideband Poisson deviance D/Nside: 0.889, 0.852 and 0.915 at excluded masses 65, 78, 120 MeV. Nside counts bins; it is not fitted degrees of freedom.

At the selected 78 MeV anchor, 237/256 source-conditional refitted toys have D at least as large as observed ; 95% Clopper–Pearson interval 0.887–0.955. This does not validate withheld bins, include source uncertainty, or provide an unconditional model-goodness-of-fit probability.
The previous held-out Q/Nbin diagnostic is distinct; its v5.9.5 conditional mean spans 0.998–1.185. Do not transfer that statistic's interpretation to the new sideband deviance.

new_after_source23.title: Validation: evidence and remaining limits

rows.heading: Window and recovery
rows.body: ±2.25σ training/extraction; refined 65 MeV tests recover 96.6–96.9% of the injected amplitude.

rows.heading: Spurious fitted yield
rows.body: 20/20 background-only mean pulls lie within ±0.5, a tolerance chosen after seeing the results.

rows.heading: Returned uncertainty
rows.body: 15/80 all-strength 90% pull-width intervals exclude 1; retain those departures.

rows.heading: Separate fixed-source check
rows.body: At 78 MeV, the 2021 signed-root mean is 0.548 in 256 null toys; it is not centered at zero.

new_after_source23.footer: Checks constrain the tested sources. Background-source uncertainty and confidence-limit coverage remain open.
notes: The first three rows are historical analytic-source validation; the last row is the distinct v5.9.5 frozen-source, fixed-kernel 2021 native 10% audit.
The 65 MeV recovery is paired across shared background realizations at input strengths 1, 3, 5; the residual amplitude loss is 3.1–3.4%. It is not coverage.
3/20 zero-signal and 15/80 all-strength normal-theory 90% width intervals exclude 1. These correlated intervals are diagnostics, not 15 independent failures.
The 78 MeV null mean 0.547975 has MC standard error about 0.0632; the source-Asimov signed root a=0.576784. A positive scan maximum is separately expected from maximization.
Low-mass qualifications include native 10% 65 MeV negative offset and 55 MeV under-recovery. The post-result ±0.5 benchmark is practical tolerance, not a prespecified zero-bias test.
Do not equate the 20 or 80 historical pull summaries with the 256 complete-source scans in the latest audit.

slide22.title: Signal Injection
slide22.subtitle: Choose the yield before injection
steps: Fit this background-only toy at this mass; record its signal-yield error σA,ref.
Add the full Gaussian signal template to the same background toy at the chosen yield.
Rerun the GP sideband fit and signed extraction; keep the injected yield fixed.
slide22.footer: z sets an input yield, not the measured significance. The pull uses the error returned after injection.
slide22.notes: Reference is matched by source, toy and mass, using the same support, mask, binning and fit settings. It is not a universal error shared by all toys. Strengths reuse the background realization and are correlated. No fresh independent Poisson(B+S) drawing rule is claimed. The full template is not renormalized only within the extraction window.
